quests.question: The flight was delayed ___ a mechanical issue.
quests.targetSentence: The flight was delayed because of a mechanical issue.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Because of' is a fixed two-word preposition introducing the cause of something, here a mechanical issue.
quests.nativeTip: This introduces the cause of a problem, made up of two words together.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'because of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The flight was delayed because of a mechanical issue.'

quests.question: The trip was cancelled ___ the storm warning.
quests.targetSentence: The trip was cancelled because of the storm warning.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Because of' fits again here, connecting an event — the cancellation — to the reason behind it.
quests.nativeTip: This links the cancellation directly to its cause.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'because of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The trip was cancelled because of the storm warning.'

quests.question: He couldn't attend the meeting ___ a family emergency.
quests.targetSentence: He couldn't attend the meeting because of a family emergency.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Because of' completes the pattern once more, introducing a reason for someone's absence.
quests.nativeTip: The same cause-and-effect pattern from the earlier examples applies here too.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'because of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'He couldn't attend the meeting because of a family emergency.'

quests.question: Let's take the scenic route ___ the highway today.
quests.targetSentence: Let's take the scenic route instead of the highway today.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Instead of' shows one option being chosen in place of another; 'rather' alone is incomplete without 'than'.
quests.nativeTip: This shows one option replacing another, and needs both its words to work.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'instead of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Let's take the scenic route instead of the highway today.'

quests.question: She ordered a salad ___ fries with her meal.
quests.targetSentence: She ordered a salad instead of fries with her meal.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Instead of' shows a substitution — the salad replaces the fries; 'besides' would mean an addition, not a swap.
quests.nativeTip: One dish replaces another here, not an addition or an exception.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'instead of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'She ordered a salad instead of fries with her meal.'

quests.question: He decided to walk to work ___ driving, to save money on gas.
quests.targetSentence: He decided to walk to work instead of driving, to save money on gas.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Instead of' completes the substitution pattern once more — walking replaces driving.
quests.nativeTip: Walking is chosen in place of another option, following the same pattern as the earlier examples.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'instead of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'He decided to walk to work instead of driving, to save money on gas.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: despite vs in spite of
quests.question: The outdoor concert went ahead as planned, ___ the heavy rain.
quests.targetSentence: The outdoor concert went ahead as planned, despite the heavy rain.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: despite vs in spite of
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Despite' stands alone, with no 'of' following it — 'despite of' is a very common but incorrect form.
quests.nativeTip: This single word never takes 'of' after it, unlike its longer twin phrase.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'despite' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The outdoor concert went ahead as planned, despite the heavy rain.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: despite vs in spite of
quests.question: She finished the marathon ___ a painful ankle injury.
quests.targetSentence: She finished the marathon in spite of a painful ankle injury.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: despite vs in spite of
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In spite of' always includes 'of' as its final word; 'despite of' incorrectly combines both forms into one mistaken phrase.
quests.nativeTip: This three-word phrase always needs its final word, unlike its shorter twin.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in spite of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'She finished the marathon in spite of a painful ankle injury.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: despite vs in spite of
quests.question: He was offered the position ___ his lack of experience.
quests.targetSentence: He was offered the position despite his lack of experience.
quests.grammarRule: Contrast: despite vs in spite of
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Despite' is correct and needs no 'of'; 'in spite' alone is also wrong, since that phrase requires 'of' to be complete.
quests.nativeTip: Watch out for two opposite mistakes: adding 'of' where it doesn't belong, or dropping it where it's required.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'despite' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'He was offered the position despite his lack of experience.'

quests.question: It should be sunny all weekend, ___ the weather forecast.
quests.targetSentence: It should be sunny all weekend, according to the weather forecast.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'According to' introduces the source of information or a reported claim, here the forecast.
quests.nativeTip: This reports a claim from a specific source, not a cause.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'according to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'It should be sunny all weekend, according to the weather forecast.'

quests.question: All visitors must sign in at reception, ___ company policy.
quests.targetSentence: All visitors must sign in at reception, according to company policy.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'According to' fits again, attributing a rule to the document or policy that states it.
quests.nativeTip: A rule is being attributed to its written source here, not its cause.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'according to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'All visitors must sign in at reception, according to company policy.'

quests.question: The bridge is completely safe, ___ the engineer's official report.
quests.targetSentence: The bridge is completely safe, according to the engineer's official report.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'According to' introduces the report as the source of the claim, unlike 'thanks to', which would credit the report as the cause of the bridge's safety.
quests.nativeTip: A report is a source of a claim, not the reason something is true.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'according to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The bridge is completely safe, according to the engineer's official report.'

quests.question: The game was postponed ___ severe weather conditions.
quests.targetSentence: The game was postponed due to severe weather conditions.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Due to' is a fixed multiword preposition meaning 'caused by'; 'because' alone is incomplete without 'of'.
quests.nativeTip: This two-word phrase needs both words to work correctly.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'due to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The game was postponed due to severe weather conditions.'

quests.question: The delay was due ___ a technical fault in the system.
quests.targetSentence: The delay was due to a technical fault in the system.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Due' is always followed by 'to', never 'of', 'for', or 'with', when explaining a cause.
quests.nativeTip: 'Due' always pairs with the same single word to form this phrase.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The delay was due to a technical fault in the system.'

quests.question: Prices have risen sharply this month ___ a sudden increase in demand.
quests.targetSentence: Prices have risen sharply this month due to a sudden increase in demand.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Due to' is correct and complete; 'owing' alone is incomplete without 'to', the same kind of error as 'because' without 'of'.
quests.nativeTip: Two related phrases both get shortened incorrectly by learners — this one drops its second word by mistake.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'due to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Prices have risen sharply this month due to a sudden increase in demand.'

quests.question: She receives a generous travel allowance ___ her salary.
quests.targetSentence: She receives a generous travel allowance in addition to her salary.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In addition to' introduces something extra alongside what's already mentioned, unlike 'instead of', which would replace it.
quests.nativeTip: Something extra is being added here, not replaced or explained.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in addition to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'She receives a generous travel allowance in addition to her salary.'

quests.question: She's a skilled painter, ___ being a talented musician.
quests.targetSentence: She's a skilled painter, in addition to being a talented musician.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In addition to' fits again, adding one quality to another rather than replacing or explaining it.
quests.nativeTip: Two talents are being combined here, not contrasted.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in addition to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'She's a skilled painter, in addition to being a talented musician.'

quests.question: The hotel offers free breakfast ___ a complimentary shuttle service to the airport.
quests.targetSentence: The hotel offers free breakfast in addition to a complimentary shuttle service to the airport.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In addition to' completes the pattern once more, listing an extra benefit alongside another.
quests.nativeTip: Two hotel perks are being listed together here.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in addition to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The hotel offers free breakfast in addition to a complimentary shuttle service to the airport.'

quests.question: I'm writing this email ___ my manager, who is currently on leave.
quests.targetSentence: I'm writing this email on behalf of my manager, who is currently on leave.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'On behalf of' means acting as someone's representative; 'in favor of' would instead mean supporting an idea or position.
quests.nativeTip: This means acting or speaking as someone's representative.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'on behalf of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'I'm writing this email on behalf of my manager, who is currently on leave.'

quests.question: The lawyer will speak ___ her client during the hearing.
quests.targetSentence: The lawyer will speak on behalf of her client during the hearing.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'On behalf of' fits again, showing the lawyer is representing the client's interests.
quests.nativeTip: The lawyer represents someone else's interests here, rather than simply accompanying them.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'on behalf of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The lawyer will speak on behalf of her client during the hearing.'

quests.question: I'd like to thank you for your hard work this year, ___ the entire team.
quests.targetSentence: I'd like to thank you for your hard work this year, on behalf of the entire team.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'On behalf of' shows the speaker is representing the entire team while giving thanks.
quests.nativeTip: The speaker represents a whole group with this phrase.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'on behalf of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'I'd like to thank you for your hard work this year, on behalf of the entire team.'

quests.question: The report looks great, ___ a few minor typos.
quests.targetSentence: The report looks great, apart from a few minor typos.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Apart from' introduces an exception to an otherwise general statement, here a few small errors.
quests.nativeTip: This introduces a small exception to an otherwise positive statement.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'apart from' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The report looks great, apart from a few minor typos.'

quests.question: I can't see any downside to this plan, ___ the cost.
quests.targetSentence: I can't see any downside to this plan, apart from the cost.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Apart from' fits again, naming the one exception to an otherwise favorable view.
quests.nativeTip: One exception is carved out of an otherwise positive opinion.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'apart from' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'I can't see any downside to this plan, apart from the cost.'

quests.question: Nobody else showed up to the meeting ___ two junior staff members.
quests.targetSentence: Nobody else showed up to the meeting apart from two junior staff members.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Apart from' completes the exception pattern once more, naming who showed up when almost no one else did.
quests.nativeTip: Two people are the exception to an otherwise empty room.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'apart from' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Nobody else showed up to the meeting apart from two junior staff members.'

quests.question: Please bring your ID ___ two passport photos to the appointment.
quests.targetSentence: Please bring your ID along with two passport photos to the appointment.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Along with' means 'together with', combining two required items; 'apart from' would instead mean excluding something.
quests.nativeTip: Two items are needed together here, not one instead of the other.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'along with' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Please bring your ID along with two passport photos to the appointment.'

quests.question: The manager, ___ two senior engineers, will review the proposal tomorrow.
quests.targetSentence: The manager, along with two senior engineers, will review the proposal tomorrow.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Along with' fits again, showing the manager is joined by two colleagues.
quests.nativeTip: Several people are attending together here.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'along with' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The manager, along with two senior engineers, will review the proposal tomorrow.'

quests.question: She packed her laptop ___ a few chargers for the trip.
quests.targetSentence: She packed her laptop along with a few chargers for the trip.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Along with' completes the pattern once more, listing items packed together.
quests.nativeTip: Multiple items are being packed together for the same trip.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'along with' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'She packed her laptop along with a few chargers for the trip.'

quests.question: Nobody was hurt in the accident, ___ your quick thinking.
quests.targetSentence: Nobody was hurt in the accident, thanks to your quick thinking.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Thanks to' credits someone or something for causing a positive outcome, here quick thinking preventing injury.
quests.nativeTip: This credits someone's positive action for a good outcome.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'thanks to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Nobody was hurt in the accident, thanks to your quick thinking.'

quests.question: The project failed ___ a lack of proper planning, not lack of effort.
quests.targetSentence: The project failed due to a lack of proper planning, not lack of effort.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Due to' fits a neutral or negative cause; 'thanks to' wouldn't fit here since it usually credits something positive.
quests.nativeTip: This introduces the cause of a negative outcome, unlike the phrase used for the positive example earlier.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'due to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The project failed due to a lack of proper planning, not lack of effort.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: because of vs despite
quests.question: David had to make the final decision on his own, ___ his manager's absence.
quests.targetSentence: David had to make the final decision on his own, because of his manager's absence.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Because of' introduces the cause of the situation; 'despite' or 'in spite of' would instead suggest the decision happened even though the manager was present, the opposite meaning.
quests.nativeTip: The absence is the reason for the decision, not something happening in spite of it.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'because of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'David had to make the final decision on his own, because of his manager's absence.'
